title: the-librarian-publishes-its-trees-client
intention: The graph-tree store in cairn/devices/librarian/trees.py becomes a client tool the librarian publishes, cairn/devices/librarian/tools/trees/trees.py, whose charter declares published_by_device and public_interface ['cairn.devices.librarian.tools.trees.trees']; the LibrarianDevice class moves out of it to cairn/devices/librarian/device.py, and RESOLUTION_FLOOR moves from librarian/loop.py into the tool, so every tenant (cairn/tools/tree, the orient and inspector nexi, codemother's chart machines, skills/moreabout) reaches the trees through the published tool and never into the librarian's insides.
why: RULE 1 child: 16 encapsulation rows reach into the librarian for its graph-tree store and its resolution floor; a client tool the librarian publishes is the declared interface
traces_to: RULE 1 (encapsulation — a device's public interface is the bus plus any client tool it publishes) via parent 8e3474a6ae43; Law 6 (the librarian owns the shared node and embedding tables; each tenant owns its leaf table through db_domain's owner gate — unchanged by the move).
how: Measured 2026-10-02 (encapsulation_breaches('.') in cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py): 128 rows; 13 land on cairn.devices.librarian.trees (cairn/tools/tree/tree.py:58, its proof, cairn/tools/orient's and build_inspector's nexus proofs, the seven codemother chart-machine proofs, codemother's test_deposit, skills/moreabout's proof) and 3 on cairn.devices.librarian.loop, every one importing RESOLUTION_FLOOR (tree.py:59, its proof, moreabout's proof). trees.py imports only cairn.tools.base.device (for LibrarianDevice at line 1244) and the db_domain client tool; its functions take an owner and a table, so each tenant's leaf table stays the tenant's, and the shared node and embedding tables stay the librarian's (Law 6). The precedent is db_domain's client (ticket 4cbf6e28126e): a device publishes a nested client tool when graph-tree volume is too heavy for a bus round trip per row. So: git mv trees.py to cairn/devices/librarian/tools/trees/trees.py; cut the device section (from '# ── the device ──' to end) into cairn/devices/librarian/device.py; move RESOLUTION_FLOOR = 0.65 and its comment into the tool, loop.py importing it back; rewrite every importer (17 'from cairn.devices.librarian import trees', 22 'from cairn.devices.librarian.trees import', 1 'import cairn.devices.librarian.trees as trees', LibrarianDevice importers to cairn.devices.librarian.device); write the tool charter through the door. The other tools-reach-devices-over-the-bus rows (operator_inbox -> trouble, codemother.dashboard, harbor_master; system_word -> ground_loop.cli, harbor_master, sudo_relay; tools/base -> bus) are not this ticket's.
falsifier: RED if: (1) the live encapsulation_breaches('.') carries any row whose module is cairn.devices.librarian.trees or cairn.devices.librarian.loop; (2) any .py file names the module cairn.devices.librarian.trees (dotted, or 'from cairn.devices.librarian import trees'), or cairn/devices/librarian/trees.py exists, or the tool module defines a class LibrarianDevice; (3) cairn/devices/librarian/tools/trees/intention+why.json does not carry published_by_device true and public_interface exactly ['cairn.devices.librarian.tools.trees.trees'], or the tool imports anything from cairn.devices other than cairn.devices.db_domain.tools.client, or it does not expose deposit, nearest, neighbors, scratch_leaf, NODES and RESOLUTION_FLOOR, or cairn.devices.librarian.loop.RESOLUTION_FLOOR is not the tool's value, or cairn.devices.librarian.device.LibrarianDevice is missing. WRONG INTENT if a tenant needs the librarian to ACT (not just store) where a client tool cannot carry it. Horizon: the tester seal of cairn/devices/librarian/tools/trees/proofs/test_trees_is_a_published_tool.py.
watchme: none, because the encapsulation_holds sieve in cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py reds any new reach into the librarian at the next inspect, and the store's behaviour is exercised by every proof that already deposits or walks
children: none, because the move is one file split in two plus a dotted-path rewrite; the other tools-reach-devices-over-the-bus clusters are siblings cast as reached
builder_notes: A Haiku builder would ask: (1) Where? git mv cairn/devices/librarian/trees.py cairn/devices/librarian/tools/trees/trees.py; empty __init__.py in tools/ and tools/trees/; the device section moves to cairn/devices/librarian/device.py. (2) What? sed the three import forms to the tool's path; LibrarianDevice importers to cairn.devices.librarian.device. (3) Proof? cairn/devices/librarian/tools/trees/proofs/test_trees_is_a_published_tool.py, PROVES keys 1, 2, 3, red first.

chart_claim.filled_by: CC chart chain (orient d67ee487e408 .. validate 536b61a28822, each learned)

decisions.text: D1 THE MOVE: `git mv cairn/devices/librarian/trees.py cairn/devices/librarian/tools/trees/trees.py`, and create empty cairn/devices/librarian/tools/__init__.py and cairn/devices/librarian/tools/trees/__init__.py (the db_domain/tools/client precedent has both). The module's bytes above the line '# ── the device ──' (trees.py:1241) are unchanged except D3.

D2 THE DEVICE CUT: everything from the '# ── the device ──' line (1241) to the end of the file (1426) moves verbatim into a new cairn/devices/librarian/device.py. That file opens with a one-paragraph docstring naming the librarian's device class and why it left the store (RULE 1, ticket 883abe55d04c), then exactly these imports (measured 2026-10-02 by an ast walk of lines 1241-1426: every free name the class body reads, minus builtins and names it binds itself): `from __future__ import annotations`, `from datetime import datetime, timezone`, `from cairn.tools.base.device import BaseDevice`, and `from cairn.devices.librarian.tools.trees.trees import (CALVE_THRESHOLD, NODES, OWNER, _MIN_CONTENT_CHARS, contradiction_scan)`. Imports inside method bodies move with the bodies unchanged. In the tool, `from cairn.tools.base.device import BaseDevice` (line 37) is deleted, because the class was its only user; the datetime import stays (the tool uses datetime, timedelta and timezone above line 1241). If importing device.py then raises NameError, the missing name is added to the trees import above; no other module is a source.

D3 THE FLOOR: `RESOLUTION_FLOOR = 0.65` and the two comment lines directly above it (loop.py:51-53) move into the tool, placed directly after `NODES = "librarian_nodes"` (tool line 42). cairn/devices/librarian/loop.py imports it back by adding RESOLUTION_FLOOR to its existing `from cairn.devices.librarian.trees import (...)` (rewritten per D4), so loop.RESOLUTION_FLOOR still resolves and is the tool's value.

D4 THE IMPORTERS, rewritten by one scratchpad script over every .py under the repo (excluding .git): `from cairn.devices.librarian import trees` -> `from cairn.devices.librarian.tools.trees import trees`; `import cairn.devices.librarian.trees as trees` -> `import cairn.devices.librarian.tools.trees.trees as trees`; `from cairn.devices.librarian.trees import (names)` -> the same names from cairn.devices.librarian.tools.trees.trees, EXCEPT that LibrarianDevice is split onto its own line `from cairn.devices.librarian.device import LibrarianDevice` (12 importers: ask, summarize, library, live, shim, chat, and the proofs test_librarian_ask, _summarize, _chat, _library, _loop, test_proactive_callback); `from cairn.devices.librarian.loop import RESOLUTION_FLOOR` (outside the librarian) -> from cairn.devices.librarian.tools.trees.trees. Multi-line parenthesized imports are rewritten whole. Afterwards `grep -rn 'cairn.devices.librarian.trees\|librarian import trees' --include=*.py .` returns nothing, and every rewritten non-proof module imports cleanly (`PYTHONPATH=. python3 -c 'import <dotted module>'` for each, exit 0); the rewritten proofs are exercised by D6.

D5 THE CHARTER: cairn/devices/librarian/tools/trees/intention+why.json is written through the door: `cairn artifact write <abs path> --verb charter --why 'the trees tool charter, ticket 883abe55d04c' --from <file>`, where <file> holds exactly this JSON (written verbatim, no field added or changed): {  "component": "trees",  "runtime_role": "tool",  "role": "charter",  "schema_version": "v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands",  "node_class": "tool",  "node_class_role": "graph-tree client",  "published_by_device": true,  "public_interface": [   "cairn.devices.librarian.tools.trees.trees"  ],  "what": "The librarian's graph-tree store, published as a tool nested in the device: deposit, nearest, neighbors, scratch_leaf, the walks, consolidation and the thread helpers over the shared node and embedding tables, plus the vocabulary (NODES, NODES_TABLE, OWNER, RESOLUTION_FLOOR) every tenant names. Every caller outside the librarian reaches the trees through this module and nothing else of the librarian's.",  "why": "RULE 1 (Akien, 2026-10-01): every component talks to every other only through its public interface, and a device's is the bus plus any client tool it publishes. Measured before the build (encapsulation_breaches, 2026-10-02): 13 rows reached into cairn.devices.librarian.trees and 3 into cairn.devices.librarian.loop for RESOLUTION_FLOOR. The trees ship vectors on every walk, too heavy for a bus round trip per row, so the librarian publishes its store the way db_domain publishes its client (ticket 4cbf6e28126e).",  "entry": "GRAFTED by git mv from cairn/devices/librarian/trees.py, ticket 883abe55d04c, 2026-10-02. The store's bytes moved unchanged; the device class left for cairn/devices/librarian/device.py and RESOLUTION_FLOOR came in from loop.py; every importer's dotted path was rewritten.",  "invoke": "`from cairn.devices.librarian.tools.trees import trees` (or `from cairn.devices.librarian.tools.trees.trees import deposit, nearest, NODES, RESOLUTION_FLOOR, ...`). Prove: `python3 cairn/devices/librarian/tools/trees/proofs/test_trees_is_a_published_tool.py` (exit 0 = green).",  "state_and_history": "A TOOL HOLDS NO STATE OF ITS OWN (Law 6): the shared node and embedding tables are the librarian's, and each tenant's leaf table is the tenant's, gated by the owner CHECK in db_domain's store. Its design history rides the librarian device's history (cairn/devices/librarian/) under ticket 883abe55d04c; nothing beside this charter holds history.",  "proof": "proofs/test_trees_is_a_published_tool.py — three teeth, one per falsifier clause of 883abe55d04c: nothing reaches into the librarian for its trees (encapsulation_breaches carries no row on librarian.trees or librarian.loop); the old address is gone (no .py names it, the file is gone, the tool holds no device class); the tool is published (this charter's two fields, its one device import is db_domain's client, its surface, the loop reads its floor, the device class stands in the device). Names resolve late, so a hollow revert reds tooth by tooth.",  "gates": "Import gate — encapsulation_holds in build_inspector (RULE 1, ticket 56d1aff4455e) admits a reach into the librarian only through this tool, because this charter says published_by_device and names its one module. Seal: the tester seals proofs/test_trees_is_a_published_tool.py into validations/ beside it.",  "falsifier": "Red if any import outside the librarian lands on librarian code other than cairn.devices.librarian.tools.trees.trees, if anything still imports cairn.devices.librarian.trees, or if this charter stops declaring published_by_device and exactly its one module.",  "learns": "It does not; it is the store the graph trees learn ON — deposits, walks and the owner gate are fixed physics, and what learns is the librarian and the tenants that use it.",  "how_it_learns": "It does not; it is the store the graph trees learn ON — deposits, walks and the owner gate are fixed physics, and what learns is the librarian and the tenants that use it.",  "traces_to": [   "RULE 1 (encapsulation — a device's public interface is the bus plus any client tool it publishes)",   "Law 6 (the shared tables are the librarian's, each leaf table its tenant's)",   "ticket 4cbf6e28126e (db_domain's published client, the precedent)"  ],  "owner": "None of its own — a tool has users (Law 6): every component that deposits or walks a graph tree. Its code is held by the librarian, which publishes it; CC gates writes to that code and its proofs.",  "gated_by": [   "CC"  ] } The librarian's own charter is not edited.

D6 THE CHECKS: BEFORE touching any file, the builder runs each of these bare and writes down its exit code: cairn/devices/librarian/proofs/test_librarian_trees.py, test_librarian_loop.py, test_librarian_ask.py, test_librarian_chat.py, test_librarian_library.py, test_librarian_summarize.py, test_proactive_callback.py, cairn/devices/codemother/proofs/test_deposit.py, and the seven cairn/devices/codemother/machines/*/proofs/test_chart_*.py. AFTER D1-D5 it runs the same list again; every one that exited 0 before exits 0 after (a proof red before may stay red, never a new red). test_trees_is_a_published_tool.py reads 3 passed. Then the build commit; the commit hook reseals what the staged files touch.

D7 PROOF: cairn/devices/librarian/tools/trees/proofs/test_trees_is_a_published_tool.py already exists at HEAD, committed red (0/3) at 319a6528 by CC before the build. PROVES keys 1-3. The builder does not create or edit it.
